proposals.before: He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in Xiliang.
proposals.after: He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in the Hexi corridor (Xiliang).
proposals.reason: Literal 'Ganzhou in Xiliang' confuses the regional name 西涼 with the person name Xiliang; idiomatic correctly treats it as the Hexi/Ganzhou region.

proposals.before: Ariq Böke sent his general Arighai from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.
proposals.after: Ariq Böke sent his general Alamdar from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 阿藍答兒 is Alamdar, not Arighai; the English conflates him with later 阿魯忽.

proposals.before: Ariq Böke sent the great general Arighai from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
proposals.after: Ariq Böke sent the great general Alamdar from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 阿藍答兒 as Arighai in the literal field.

proposals.before: Arighai asked, "Where is your father?"
proposals.after: Alamdar asked, "Where is your father?"
proposals.reason: Speaker is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar), not Arighai.

proposals.before: Arighai asked: "Where is your father?"
proposals.after: Alamdar asked: "Where is your father?"
proposals.reason: Speaker is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar), not Arighai.

proposals.before: Arighai fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a pointed meaning."
proposals.after: Alamdar fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a pointed meaning."
proposals.reason: Speaker is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar).

proposals.before: Arighai stared intently at Hunduhai and said: "These words carry deep meaning."
proposals.after: Alamdar stared intently at Hunduhai and said: "These words carry deep meaning."
proposals.reason: Speaker is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar).

proposals.before: Arighai accepted this as the truth and lifted the close guard over him.
proposals.after: Alamdar accepted this as the truth and lifted the close guard over him.
proposals.reason: Subject is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar).

proposals.before: Arighai took this as truth and released him from close guard.
proposals.after: Alamdar took this as truth and released him from close guard.
proposals.reason: Subject is 阿藍答兒 (Alamdar).

proposals.before: Before long Arighai and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Hala Buqa as their leader.
proposals.after: Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Hala Buqa as their leader.
proposals.reason: 阿藍答兒 should be Alamdar, not Arighai.

proposals.before: Before long Arighai and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Hala Buqa commander.
proposals.after: Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Hala Buqa commander.
proposals.reason: 阿藍答兒 should be Alamdar, not Arighai.

proposals.before: Prince Arighai then arrived, executed Suoluohai, Ariq Böke's garrison commander, and declared his intent to join Kublai.
proposals.after: Prince Alughu then arrived, executed Suoluohai, Ariq Böke's garrison commander, and declared his intent to join Kublai.
proposals.reason: Chinese 阿魯忽 is Alughu, distinct from 阿藍答兒; English wrongly uses Arighai.

proposals.before: When Prince Arighai arrived, he executed Suoluohai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in charge of the garrison, wishing to attach himself to the Shizu Emperor.
proposals.after: When Prince Alughu arrived, he executed Suoluohai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in charge of the garrison, wishing to attach himself to the Shizu Emperor.
proposals.reason: 宗王阿魯忽 is Alughu, not Arighai.

proposals.before: He again followed Princes Daming and Arighai back to Yemili.
proposals.after: He again followed Princes Daming and Alughu back to Yemili.
proposals.reason: Second prince is 阿魯忽 (Alughu), not Arighai.

proposals.before: He again followed the two princes Daming Wang and Arighai back to Yemili City.
proposals.after: He again followed the two princes Daming Wang and Alughu back to Yemili City.
proposals.reason: 阿魯忽 should be Alughu.

proposals.before: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili, the appanage town assigned to Ögedei when he was still heir apparent.
proposals.after: In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili, the appanage town of Güyük before he became khan.
proposals.reason: 定宗 is Güyük, not Ögedei; 潛邸 identifies his pre-accession appanage.

proposals.before: In the third year Prince Daming, Ögedei's youngest son, took pity on his inability to return home and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.
proposals.after: In the third year Prince Daming, Güyük's youngest son, took pity on his inability to return home and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.
proposals.reason: 定宗 is Güyük, so Prince Daming is identified here as Güyük’s youngest son.

proposals.before: He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty and Upholds Righteousness, Zishan dafu, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui with the posthumous name Zhongjia.
proposals.after: He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Supports Righteousness, and Upholds Integrity, Zishan dafu, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui Commandery with the posthumous name Zhongjia.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits 守正 from 推忠輔義守正功臣 and drops 郡 from 漆水郡公, both present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: His father Heizi inherited the marshal's post through hereditary service and also held the post of darughachi of the Wenzou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.
proposals.after: His father Heizi inherited the marshal's post through hereditary service and also held the post of darughachi of the Wenzhou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.
proposals.reason: 文州 is Wenzhou; idiomatic Wenzou is a corrupted romanization that obscures the place name.

proposals.before: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Fengyi dafu and dispatched as administrator of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit Surveillance Commission.
proposals.after: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Fengyi dafu and dispatched as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
proposals.reason: Chinese 江南湖北道 is Jiangnan Hubei Circuit; Huguang (湖廣) is a different toponym.

proposals.before: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Fengyi dafu and sent out as administrator of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit Surveillance Commission.
proposals.after: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Fengyi dafu and sent out as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
proposals.reason: Chinese 江南湖北道 is Jiangnan Hubei Circuit; the literal likewise misrenders 湖北 as Huguang.

proposals.before: He was soon promoted to Hanlin expositor-in-chief while retaining the censorate, but Shiyan firmly declined the latter and was relieved of it.
proposals.after: He was soon promoted to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts while retaining the censor-in-chief post, but Shiyan firmly declined the latter and was relieved of it.
proposals.reason: 翰林學士承旨 is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts; idiomatic drops 學士 and understates concurrent 御史中丞.

proposals.before: Temuder reported other charges, had him imprisoned, and pressed him to kill himself. Shiyan did not waver and spent two years in prison.
proposals.after: Temuder reported other charges to the emperor, had him imprisoned in the penal office, and pressed him to kill himself. Shiyan did not waver and spent two years in prison.
proposals.reason: Chinese 白帝 and 系之刑曹 state that Temuder reported to the emperor and imprisoned Shiyan in the penal office; the idiomatic omits both.

proposals.before: Left Chancellor Bayiju repeatedly said Shiyan was innocent; he received an order to leave prison and recuperate at his residence.
proposals.after: Left Chancellor Bayiju repeatedly said Shiyan was innocent; an order released Shiyan from prison to recuperate at his residence.
proposals.reason: Chinese 得旨出獄 refers to Shiyan's release, not Bayiju receiving the order; the literal pronoun wrongly points to Bayiju.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he came to court, was again made censor-in-chief, and was promoted to right chancellor of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he came to court, was again made censor-in-chief, and was promoted to right vice chancellor of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Chinese 中書右丞 is the Secretariat Right Vice Chancellor, not the higher Right Chancellor (右丞相).

proposals.before: In the fourth year he entered court, again became censor-in-chief, and was further transferred to right chancellor of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he entered court, again became censor-in-chief, and was further transferred to right vice chancellor of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Chinese 中書右丞 is the Secretariat Right Vice Chancellor, not the higher Right Chancellor (右丞相).

proposals.before: In the fifth month of the next year he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, enjoying seventy-seven years.
proposals.after: In the fifth month of the next year he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, aged seventy-seven.
proposals.reason: Literal 享年 calque 'enjoying … years' is unnatural English and obscures the age-at-death sense.

proposals.before: Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit—in the early Tianli reign Nanggal Tai seized Shu in rebellion and died in the turmoil; he was specially granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died for the Cause, Zishan dafu, Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Shu Commandery; posthumous name Zhongmin.
proposals.after: Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit—in the early Tianli reign Nanggal Tai seized Shu in rebellion and Bohu died in the turmoil; he was specially granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died for the Cause, Zishan dafu, Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Shu Commandery; posthumous name Zhongmin.
proposals.reason: Literal English leaves “died in the turmoil” ambiguous between Nanggal Tai and Bohu; the Chinese narrative and following posthumous honors show Bohu is the one who died.

proposals.before: In the Dazhong period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.
proposals.after: In the Zhida period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.
proposals.reason: Chinese 至大中 is the Yuan Zhida reign (AD 1308–1311), not Dazhong; the idiomatic English misnames the reign.

proposals.before: In the Dazhong period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor of the Fanyang Confucian school.
proposals.after: In the Zhida period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor of the Fanyang Confucian school.
proposals.reason: Chinese 至大中 is Zhida, not Dazhong; the literal English misnames the reign.

proposals.before: An edict then enfeoffed the Sage's father as King Qisheng and his mother as Lady Wang.
proposals.after: An edict then enfeoffed the Sage's father as King Qisheng and his mother as royal consort.
proposals.reason: 王夫人 here is the consort title of a king (夫人 of a 王), not a personal name Lady Wang.

proposals.before: An edict then added the enfeoffment of the Sage's father as King Qisheng and the Sage's mother as Lady Wang.
proposals.after: An edict then added the enfeoffment of the Sage's father as King Qisheng and the Sage's mother as royal consort.
proposals.reason: 王夫人 is a royal-consort title after the father was made king, not the surname-title Lady Wang.

s0178 享年七十有七 means he died aged seventy-seven; “enjoying seventy-seven years” is a misleading calque of 享年.
s0185 topic is 伯忽; 死於難 and the following posthumous honors refer to Bohu, not Nanggal Tai. Naming Bohu removes the false ambiguity.
s0194 至大中 is the Yuan Zhida reign, not Dazhong; the idiomatic misnames the era.
s0194 literal likewise misreads 至大 as Dazhong; Zhida is the correct reign name.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0002 makes Alamdar the personal name for 阿藍答兒; the alternate-name claim existed only to salvage the correct form beside the bad Arighai personal name.
Accepted r0012 makes Alughu the personal name for 阿魯忽; the alternate-name claim was only a salvage beside the bad Arighai personal name.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0002 shows English Arighai for 阿藍答兒 came only from the bad translation; the personal-name claim must read Alamdar.
Accepted r0012 shows English Arighai for 阿魯忽 came only from the bad translation; the personal-name claim must read Alughu.
Accepted r0012 restores 宗王阿魯忽 as Prince Alughu; Prince Arighai was produced only by the bad translation.
